sentences.text: This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:

On 04.02.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding a motor cycle bearing No.KA-59-H-9030 towards Hinnaki and reached near Naganayakanahalli Lake, on Naganayakanahalli-Hinnaki Road, at that time, the driver of the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-6333 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and due to excessive speed the driver of the lorry lost control over his vehicle and came to the wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, as a result of which, petitioner fell down on the road sustained grievous injuries.

Further stated that petitioner took treatment at hospital and sustained grievous left Humerus fracture, deep lacerated wound in Left Knee joint and left foot and other multiple injuries and underwent multiple surgeries such as ORIF-plating- Humerus CRIF+K- wiring - Wound debridement and suture.
Post operative period was uneventful and discharged with an advice to take regular followup treatment.
The petitioner spent amount for his treatment.

Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years, he was doing Vegetable Vendor work and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries,
not able to do work from the date of accident till today.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 appeared through their respective counsel before the Tribunal and filed their respective written statement.
The respondent No.1 in his written statement contended that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the petitioner who was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-59-H-9030.
The claim made by the petitioner is exaggerated and without any basis.
4. The 2nd respondent filed its written statement contended that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
The accident caused due to sole negligence of the petitioner himself and not due to negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
The claim is bad for non-compliance of section 158(6) and 134(c) of the MV Act.
This respondent seeks protection under section 147 and 150 of MV Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.

5. From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an Madhu D vs Nandi Conmix on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38598665/
2 accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-6333 on 04.02.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. near Naganayakanahalli Lake, Naganayakanahalli-Hinnaki Road, Kasaba Hobli, Anekal,
Bengaluru City?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined one witness as PW2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P20 documents.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: In order to prove the rash and negligence, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 20 documents i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, Aadhar card, DL, discharge summary, OP case sheet, medical bills,
prescriptions, Advance bills, OPD card and X- ray.

10. The materials on record reveals that soon after the accident Petitioner himself has lodged complaint as per Ex- P2 on the basis of which Suryanagar PS registered FIR as per Ex-P1 against the driver of the offending vehicle Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-6333.

Thereafter jurisdictional police conducted thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per Ex-P6 against the driver of the Lorry by name Majarul S.K., for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC by holding that on 04.02.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., the accused was driving the Concrete Mixer Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-B-6333 in a rash and negligent manner on Naganayakanahalli-Hinnaki Road,
Naganayakanahalli Lake, near Suryanagara 2nd Stage road and hit to the Motor cycle ridden by the petitioner along with one Madan as a pillion rider, due to the impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Though respondent No.1 and 2 disputed the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, but neither respondent No.1 nor respondent No.2 examined the driver of the vehicle to prove their contention or to disprove the evidence of PW-1.
Even respondent has not challenged and disputed all the police documents produced by the petitioner.

There are no other Madhu D vs Nandi Conmix on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38598665/
3 evidence and materials to prove that the Ex-P9-charge sheet filed by the petitioner is collusive and defective.
11. On perusal of the Ex-P3 Spot mahazar, it clearly shows that in the spot of accident, the road was running North-South direction.
The accident has been taken place in the circle where four roads join and the accident occurred in the road attached to the Suryanagara Face-2.

Further it clearly shows that when the petitioner was riding the Motor cycle from Naganayakanahalli towards Hinnaki, at that time, the driver of the Lorry came in a rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and hit to the petitioner.
The Ex.P3 clearly shows that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.4 IMV report also clearly shows that the damages were caused to the front portion of the Motor cycle and also front portion of the Lorry which also corroborates the nature and cause of accident.
12. Though learned counsel for the respondent cross examined PW-1 at length, but nothing was elicited from his mouth.
PW-1 has outrightly denied the suggestions made by the respondent counsel with regard to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner.
Even there are no materials to prove that the charge sheet is defective and collusive.
All these documents clearly shows that the car was involved in the accident.
Moreover all these documents have not at all been disputed by the respondents.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.

15. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the offending vehicle.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Madhu D vs Nandi Conmix on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38598665/
4 17. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 22 years.
The petitioner has produced aadhaar card and DL as per Ex-P7 and 8, it reveals the date of birth of the petitioner was 16.08.2000.
So, as on the date of accident 04.02.2022 the petitioner was aged 22 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing Vegetable vendor work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,500/-
p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-

As per the medical records i.e., Ex-P5- wound certificate reveals that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1) Lacerated wound over left Ankle (2) Lacerated wound over left foot over Tendo arthrities (3) Fracture shaft and Head of left humerus and the doctor has opined that the injuries No.2 and 3 are grievous in nature and injury No.1 is simple in nature.

Ex-P9-discharge summary of BEST hospital, Bengaluru reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 4 days i.e., from 04.02.2022 to 07.02.2022.
19.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr. S.A. Somashekara as PW-2 who has stated that petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., Fracture shaft and Head of left humerus, Lacerated wound over left Ankle and Lacerated wound over left foot over Tendo arthrities and underwent surgeries i.e., ORIF with plating for shaft of Humerus fracture CRIF with K-wiring proximal Humerus fracture and Wound debridement and closure on 04.02.2022 and he was treated as inpatient and discharged from the hospital on 07-02-2022 with advice of followup and petitioner used to attend regularly.
PW-2 further stated that he examined the petitioner and petitioner complaints of painand difficulty in using Left upper limb for activities of daily living.
History of inability to lift weight and carry out over head activities.
History of inability to squat and sit cross legged.
On examination he has surgical scars mark over left shoulder and left ankle, Wasting of left upper limb and Secondary scars and contractures over left tendo arthrities.
PW-2 further stated that x-ray of head, shows united fracture proximal humerus and united fracture shaft of Humerus with implants in situ.
PW-2 assessed the total disability of both limbs at 37% and whole body at 19%.
PW-2 produced Ex-P19-OPD card and Ex.P.20-X-ray.
19. During cross examination of PW.2 admitted that bones are united.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.

Madhu D vs Nandi Conmix on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38598665/
5 20.

Considering the nature of injuries, age of petitioner, occupation of petitioner, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner working as a Vegetable vendor, certainly has to face some difficulty and disability to carry his avocation.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 15%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/-p.m.

Hence a sum of Rs.5,02,200/-
(Rs.15,500 X 12 X 18 X 15/100) is awarded under this head.
21. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1) Lacerated wound over left Ankle (2) Lacerated wound over left foot over Tendo arthrities (3) Fracture shaft and Head of left humerus and the doctor has opined that the injuries No.2 and 3 are grievous in nature and injury No.1 is simple in nature.
Ex-P9-discharge summary of BEST hospital, Bengaluru reveals that petitioner took treatment as inpatient for 4 days i.e., from 04.02.2022 to 07.02.2022.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony due to the injuries sustained by him on account of the accidental injuries.
The petitioner being 22 years, certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the BEST hospital, Bangalore for 4 days as inpatient.
Since the petitioner admitted to the hospital on 04.02.2022 complaining about the fracture shaft and Head of left humerus, Lacerated wound over left Ankle and Lacerated wound over left foot over Tendo arthrities
, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.77,500/-
(15,500 X 5) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
23. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is a resident of Naganayakanahalli,
Marsur, Anekal, Bengaluru and has taken treatment at BEST hospital, Bangalore as inpatient for total 4 days and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of treatment, the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS :
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical disability with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer Madhu D vs Nandi Conmix on 8 April, 2025
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38598665/
6 discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical prescriptions Ex-P12 and medical bills Ex-P11 for Rs.1,33,281/-.
I proceed to award Rs.1,33,281/- under the head of medical expenses.
26. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The PW-2 doctor has stated that petitioner requires surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in private set up.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove the future medical expenses.
However by considering the say of doctor this tribunal awarding Rs.40,000/- towards future medical expenses.
27. The calculation table stands as follows :

1 Loss of future income : 5,02,200=00 due to disability 2P Pain & sufferings :
1,00,000=00 3 Loss of income during : 77,500=00 laid-up period
4A Attendant charges, extra : 15,000=00 nutritious food &conveyance charges 5 Loss of future amenities & R: 25,000=00 happiness 1, 6
Medical expenses : 1,33,281=00 7
Future medical expenses : 40,000 =00 Total 8,92,981=00
Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.8,92,981/-.
28. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
29. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-6333 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
30.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

7

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,92,981=00 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioners within 30 days from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.1 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.
